candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — colorectal cancer stool screening
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the purpose and follow-up requirement of stool-based occult-blood colorectal-cancer screening.

options.A: Tests such as FIT or high-sensitivity guaiac testing look for blood in stool; an abnormal screening result requires follow-up colonoscopy.
options.B: A positive stool test by itself confirms colorectal cancer, so follow-up colonoscopy is unnecessary.
options.C: The test directly visualizes the entire colon and permits removal of polyps during the same procedure.
options.D: A negative result permanently ends the need for future colorectal-cancer screening.

candidate.rationale: USPSTF identifies FIT and high-sensitivity guaiac fecal occult-blood testing as stool-based screening methods that detect blood. An abnormal stool-based screening result requires colonoscopy for diagnostic follow-up. The stool test does not visualize the colon, confirm cancer by itself, or eliminate future screening after one negative result.
candidate.source_claim_supported: FIT and high-sensitivity gFOBT detect blood in stool; abnormal stool-based screening results require colonoscopy.
